real_estate.homebuilder: Mortgage rates climbed to 7.50% this week, about $229 a month more on the median Fremont home.
real_estate.commentary:
Mortgage News Daily's 30-year average ended the week at 7.50% Friday, up 0.33 from the Friday before and 1.16 above a year ago, with the 15-year at 7.03%. On today's $1,275,000 Fremont median with 20% down, that is about $7,132 a month in principal and interest, $229 more than at last Friday's 7.17%. Freddie Mac's weekly survey, published Thursday, came in lower at 7.11%, down 0.07; Mortgage News Daily's daily index caught Thursday's and Friday's rise in yields.

Our own board eased a little over the week (chart). From Friday to Friday, the 15 city table went from 2,464 listings to 2,419, homes in contract from 631 to 622, and the five city ledger from 628 to 623. Fremont's median on market list price slipped to $1,279,000 from $1,299,000.

Sunday's export shows 2,421 board wide, from 2,419 Friday, with 138 coming soon and 155 brand new. The five city ledger is 616, from 623: Milpitas (98) added two, while Fremont (212) fell four, Hayward (177) and Union City (57) two each, and Newark (72) one.

What this means for you: a third of a point in one week is about $229 a month on the median Fremont home, so buyers who are ready should ask their lender about locking rather than waiting for a pullback. Sellers, buyers are pricing in that payment, so price for it. Rates did not take the short week off.

• Board wide: 2,421 listings across our 15 city table, counting active and in contract together, with 138 coming soon and 155 brand new.

📍 Alameda County (Fremont Focus)

• Live ledger: 616 listings across Fremont, Hayward, Milpitas, Newark and Union City. 546 are on the market and 70 are coming soon.
• Fremont: 212 live, 165 active, 29 coming soon and 18 brand new. The median on market list price is $1,275,000 at $787 a square foot, and the typical active listing has been out 37 days.
• The rest of the ledger: Hayward 177, Milpitas 98, Newark 72, Union City 57.
• Across all five cities the median is $999,994 at $666 a square foot. 274 homes are priced under a million, and 179 have been sitting 60 days or longer.

stocks.note: Levels are Friday, November 13 at the closing bell. Markets are closed for the weekend.
stocks.news:
Stocks finished the week higher (chart). The S&P 500 gained 2.51%, the Dow 2.07% and the Nasdaq 2.27% from the Friday before, and nearly all of it came Monday, when the S&P rose 2.35%. Friday was mixed: the S&P 500 slipped 0.40% and the Nasdaq 0.91%, while the Dow edged up 0.10%.

Nvidia went the other way. The Santa Clara chipmaker closed Friday at $162.85, down 2.01% on the day and 12.75% for the week, after its board accepted chief executive Jensen Huang's resignation Wednesday. It is now 12.68% below where it started the year. A good week for the index, a long one in Santa Clara.

We checked Market Briefs' weekly scoreboard against the sources. The stock, Brent and 10-Year figures hold up; gold, the mortgage rate and Bitcoin needed correcting, and the chart shows the corrected numbers.

economy.note: Levels are Friday, November 13: the 10-Year is Treasury's close, gold and silver are COMEX December settlements, and Brent is the ICE January settlement. Markets are closed for the weekend.
economy.commentary:
The 10-Year Treasury yield closed Friday at 5.15%, up 0.29 for the week and back to its October 19 close. Consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, more than the 0.3% economists expected, with core prices up 0.3%, which keeps a December rate increase on the table.

Gold settled Friday at $3,886.30, down 4.63% for the week, and silver at $49.12, down 5.43%. Brent settled at $95.84, down 2.52% for the week but nearly unchanged Friday. Market Briefs' scoreboard had gold at $3,884, down 4.58%; the COMEX settlement is $3,886.30, down 4.63%. Fremont's price per square foot slipped about 1.4% this week; gold slipped 4.6%.

crypto.commentary: Bitcoin had the roughest week on the board. It ended Friday's stock session at $68,823, down 9.21% from the Friday before, and slid further this weekend; it is near $65,034, up 0.81% over the past 24 hours and still near its lowest since mid August, live from CoinGecko at 1:11 PM PT. Ether is near $1,822.33 and XRP near $0.96. Market Briefs' $69,556 was a Friday morning price, not a close. Crypto never closes, which this week was not a selling point.
